title: Polygon Challenge Problems Practice
description: Practice finding unknown sides and angle measures from polygon clues.

questions.question: A regular polygon has one exterior angle measuring 60 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: For a regular polygon, n = 360 divided by one exterior angle. 360 / 60 = 6.

questions.question: An exterior angle adjacent to an interior angle measures 42 degrees. Find the interior angle. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Adjacent interior and exterior angles form a straight angle, so 180 - 42 = 138.

questions.question: A convex quadrilateral has angles 75 degrees, 95 degrees, 110 degrees, and x. Which equation finds x?
questions.explanation: The interior angles of every quadrilateral add to 360 degrees.

questions.question: A hexagon has interior angles 120, 110, 130, 100, 140, and x degrees. Find x. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: A hexagon has interior angle sum (6 - 2) x 180 = 720. The known angles add to 600, so x = 120.

questions.question: A polygon with one interior angle greater than 180 degrees is non-convex.
questions.explanation: One interior angle greater than 180 degrees proves the polygon has an inward dent, so it is non-convex.

questions.question: A regular decagon has 10 sides. What is the measure of one exterior angle?
questions.explanation: For a regular decagon, one exterior angle is 360 / 10 = 36 degrees.

questions.question: A polygon has 8 sides, all angles equal, and all sides equal. What is the most precise classification?
questions.explanation: Eight sides make it an octagon. Equal sides and equal angles make it regular.

questions.question: A student says a polygon is regular because all its sides are equal. What extra information is needed?
questions.correctAnswer: The student also needs to know that all angles are equal. A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles.
questions.explanation: Equal sides alone are not enough to prove regularity; equal angles are also required.
